paper.title_en: Highly deformed rotational structure in the near-spherical nucleus <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Te</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>123</mn></mmultiscripts></math> at high spin
paper.abstract_en: High-spin states in <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Te</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>123</mn></mmultiscripts></math> were populated in the <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi>Se</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>82</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>(</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Ca</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>48</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>,</mo><mi>α</mi><mn>3</mn><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Te</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>123</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> reaction at a beam energy of 205 MeV, and <math><mi>γ</mi></math>-ray coincidence events were measured with the Gammasphere array. The level scheme has been extended to spin <math><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>50</mn></mrow></math> through the identification of several new <math><mi>γ</mi></math>-ray transitions, and a rotational band feeding states above <math><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>20</mn></mrow></math>. Cranked Nilsson-Strutinsky calculations are consistent with the observed low-spin yrast structure and support an interpretation of the high-spin band as a smooth terminating configuration involving two <math><msub><mi>g</mi><mrow><mn>9</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> proton holes and no neutron excitations across the <math><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>82</mn></mrow></math> shell gap. A transition from near-prolate to triaxial rotation about the intermediate axis is suggested for the band near <math><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>40</mn></mrow></math>.
